newsitem.title: USA: Sprint, Global One in global intranet pact.
newsitem.headline: Sprint, Global One in global intranet pact.

text.p: Sprint Corp and its Global One partners, including Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom, said Tuesday they had formed a worldwide alliance to offer intranet services.

The services will allow multinational companies to employ Internet and World Wide Web technologies for use in their own networks. The services are intended to create a "single, worldwide, multipoint environment for information sharing and electronic commerce," the companies said in a press release.

Sprint, Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom will market the Global Intranet to large, multinational corporations in their respective countries, while Global One will market the service in the rest of the world, the companies said.
Trials will begin with selected customers in the first quarter of 1997, and full service will be available in mid-1997.

Global Intranet will benefit from the existing Internet strength of the partners, including access in 70 countries and remote dial access in 2,350 cities throughout Europe, the United States, the Americas, Russia, the Middle East, Africa and the Asia/Pacific region.

It will provide security, directory services, electronic messaging, access to databases, seamless connections with disparate messaging systems, web-based document and information retrieval, and professional services, the companies said.

Companies in the aviation, automotive, healthcare, publishing and technology industries are turning to intranets to accelerate their speed to market, reduce communications costs, enhance communications among employees and customers, and boost productivity.

"The power of Global Intranet is that it will make global communications simpler and easier by allowing worldwide business communities to form and conduct business regardless of time zones, location or existing systems," Sprint Chairman William Esrey said in a statement.

Sprint is a global communications company, with $12.8 billion in annual revenues. Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecommunications company, with 1995 revenue of $43.5 billion. France Telecom is the fourth largest telecommunications carrier.
